items.comment: The doc undersells the message content and misses a real branch of behavior. It says the message 'names the object's class unless the object is `null`', implying the class name is the defining content for non-null objects. But `objString` (line 27-35) actually builds `s"$obj ($ofClass)"` — the object's own `toString()` followed by the class name in parentheses, e.g. `5 (of class java.lang.Integer)` — so the toString representation, not just the class name, is the prominent part of the message. The doc also omits the fallback branch: if `obj.toString` throws, the message becomes `"an instance of class " + ofClass` (no object representation at all). A reader relying on this Scaladoc would reasonably expect the message to be essentially just a class name, which is materially wrong for the common case.
